clusters.name: Walter's move of the family across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, Walter's long days away in the trees and distance from June, Glen's fights at school, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June's weeks in bed that first winter, and rows between Walter and June over money for new trees. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, marking where the family settled into the new place.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the frost took the crop and the bank called the loan: Walter drank heavily, he and Glen blamed each other, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma worsened that winter, and Nora began wetting the bed. Ida's heart trouble was found around the same time. By October 1969, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, marking where the crisis eased.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975 when the Ridgeport cannery closed: Glen sat in the truck for hours out of work most of that year, he and Marian fought loudly over money at night, Marian took a second job cleaning offices, Nora stopped eating and lost weight that summer, she kept to her room and distanced from her mother, and Walter drank again after six years off it. By June 1976, Nora was eating again and made the track team, and Glen started the delivery job in March, marking where the family turned.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990: Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, Hollis worked late and kept out of the rows, Hollis took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over Lily's care, Nora's eczema flared on both hands, and she and Hollis rowed most nights. By June 1991, Wilma took a flat in town, and over that summer Nora's eczema cleared, marking where the household settled.
